newsitem.title: UK: UK to privatise London Underground.
newsitem.headline: UK to privatise London Underground.

text.p: Transport Secretary Sir George Young confirmed on Tuesday that the Conservative government will privatise London's underground railway network if it wins Britain's coming election.
Young told parliament that the government would publish a policy white paper in the summer setting out the details of its sell-off proposals.

The minister said that, for the first time in a privatisation, proceeds of the sell-off will be recycled into investment, ensuring that the modernisation of the underground's infrastructure is completed as soon as possible.
Buyers of the "tube" will be contractually committed to modernise the system, with a guaranteed level of support from the government to supplement the private investment.
The overall aim would be to have eliminated London Underground's investment backlog within five years of privatisation, he said.
Fares will be capped for the first time, with average fare increases pegged to the level of inflation for the first four years after the sell-off.
